measurementCandidates.what: Achar's eclipse-pair dating of the Mahābhārata war: a lunar eclipse before and a solar eclipse during the 18-day war, best fit 22 Nov 3067 BCE (also given as 16 Nov–3 Dec 3067 BCE), with alternatives 3112 BCE (Mekel) and 5561 BCE (Oak).
measurementCandidates.why: A dated eclipse pair is a testable constraint on lunar and solar ephemerides; the edition ties it to the Mahābhārata 6.2.1-3 planetary references (line 5147) and the 17 references it cites, but the result rests on a planetarium simulation and literary assumptions that the edition itself flags as Tier-W.

measurementCandidates.what: Rāma's birth configuration from Bālakāṇḍa 1.18.8-10: Chaitra, navamī tithi, Punarvasu nakṣatra, five planets exalted with Jupiter exalted; dated to 4 Dec 7323 BCE (Vartak), 10 Jan 5114 BCE (Bhatnagar) and before 12200 BCE (Oak).
measurementCandidates.why: This is the most specific planetary configuration in the file and can be tested against an ephemeris; the first two dates differ by about 2,200 years, so the configuration can discriminate between them.

measurementCandidates.what: Precession-based dates for Ṛgvedic and Brāhmaṇa-era observations: the Kṛttikās 'do not deviate' (Śatapatha 2.1.2.3, quoted as 'कृत्तिकाः न च्यवन्ते') read as about 2900 BCE by Sidharth; Tilak's Orion reading about 4000 BCE; Iyengar (2010) about 1900 BCE.
measurementCandidates.why: Each is a dated equinox-position anchor and so a constraint on an ayanāṃśa epoch; the edition gives no numeric ayanāṃśa or epoch, so these dates are the only numeric precession anchors in the file.

measurementCandidates.what: Thuban was the pole star in Vedic times, about 3000 BCE (stated without source).
measurementCandidates.why: A dated pole-star identification constrains the celestial pole's position under precession; the date is approximate and unsourced.

measurementCandidates.what: Earth's formation age stated as 4.54 ± 0.05 Gyr and attributed to Hadean zircon U-Pb dating (Jack Hills, 2014); the same figure is repeated at line 3756.
measurementCandidates.why: A numeric age is stated, but the attribution looks wrong: Jack Hills detrital zircons are at most about 4.4 Ga, while 4.54 Ga is the meteoritic (solar-system) age; check the source before use as a constraint.

measurementCandidates.what: Konārka Sun temple at 19.89°N 86.10°E (1250 CE) is said to be oriented to equinox sunrise, and its wheel-axle inclination is called '~ obliquity of the ecliptic' with no value given.
measurementCandidates.why: A claimed equinox alignment and an inclination equal to obliquity would constrain obliquity if a number were given; the text gives none, so this is qualitative only.

measurementCandidates.what: Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa's five-year counts (62 synodic, 67 sidereal months, 1830 tithi) imply a mean synodic month of 1830/62 = 29.516 days and about 366 days per year.
measurementCandidates.why: A rate constraint stated without source; the same line's 1860 days contradicts the 1830 count and should be checked before use.

measurementCandidates.what: 27 nakṣatras against the sidereal lunar period of 27.32166 days; the edition's '~1.013°' per day-equivalent is a units slip for the ratio 27.32166/27 ≈ 1.012 days per nakṣatra.
measurementCandidates.why: A rate constraint with a unit error; corrected, it is consistent with the modern sidereal month.
